title: Terraform crypto-bridge module: pluggable KMS/HSM abstraction + secrets sync to Vault/Secrets Manager
creator: Priya Singh
description: Build a reusable Terraform module (crypto-bridge) that provides a vendor-agnostic KMS/HSM abstraction and automated secrets synchronization to HashiCorp Vault and AWS Secrets Manager. The goal is to give Private deployment customers a single IaC entrypoint to: 1) provision KMS keys or HSM connectors (PKCS#11/Thales interfaces), 2) wire those keys into the Redwood control plane and private components, and 3) optionally bootstrap a secrets sync mechanism that mirrors secrets into Vault or SM with configurable rotation/ttl policies. Module must support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, and an HSM connector mode for on-prem Thales/Entrust devices.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes a single set of variables for key lifecycle: key_alias, key_policy_template, rotation_window_days, and provider_type
Support for provider_type values: aws-kms, gcp-kms, azure-kv, hsm-pkcs11
Produces outputs: key_resource_id, key_public_fingerprint, kms_connection_info (for hsm connector), terraform_state_migration_notes
Secrets sync can be enabled or disabled; when enabled: a scheduler (lambda/k8s job) or sidecar deploys to mirror specified secrets to Vault or AWS Secrets Manager
Module includes a healthcheck resource (k8s readiness probe or cloud function) that reports key availability, HSM connectivity, and last-sync timestamp
Comprehensive upgrade plan documented: 1->2 versions change for key aliasing and state migration without key rotation by default
Automated e2e test in CI that provisions a test KMS (or emulator), creates a test secret, and verifies mirror into Vault/SM
Security review sign-off completed and integration tests running in nightly pipeline

implementation_notes: Architecture: terraform module builds provider-specific resources under a common interface. For cloud providers we use native KMS resources and create an IAM role/service account for Redwood control plane access. For HSM mode we deploy a lightweight connector (containerized agent) into the customer VPC with an autoscaling group and a PKCS#11 PKI layer; terraform provisions the connector config and an encrypted secret reference in Vault. Secrets syncer: optional controller (k8s job or lambda) that reads a secrets map (secrets_to_sync var) and mirrors values to target Vault path or AWS Secrets Manager. Healthchecks: module deploys a health endpoint and CloudWatch/Prometheus metrics for last_sync_timestamp, key_status, connector_online. Upgrade path: non-destructive by default; alias mapping and a migration helper script written in Go included in the repo to move tfstate references if provider changes. See examples for recommended canary rollout: spin new connector in separate subnet, validate keywrap ops, then shift role bindings.
